text: Build the next generation of statistical programs and operations.

In 2026-27, Statistics Canada will continue to modernize its statistical programs and provide its employees with the tools and training they need to deliver on its core responsibility of providing trustworthy, objective, high-quality information for Canadians.

Underpinning Statistics Canada's efforts to maintain relevant economic and social statistics is its commitment to refining and updating its statistical methods to build the next generation of statistical programs and operations.

Emerging technologies such as AI are central to addressing many of the challenges faced by national statistical organizations and will enable Statistics Canada to build the next generation of statistical programs and operations.

These changes will build on the agency's prior strategic investments in technology, particularly in artificial intelligence, machine learning and automation, which have already been shown to improve operational efficiency and responsiveness.

text: Across Canada and within the federal public service, there is a clear expectation that institutions deliver tangible results with focus, discipline, and speed.
Leaders are being called upon to strengthen productivity, make explicit choices about priorities, and demonstrate value in practical terms.
At the same time, fiscal realities require thoughtful stewardship and sharper alignment of resources to outcomes.

For Statistics Canada, this context demands an agenda that is both ambitious and deliberate—one that reinforces operational excellence, accelerates modernization, strengthens our digital and methodological foundations, and equips our people to execute with clarity and confidence.
The Economic Statistics Field plays a critical role in this agenda.

As the producer of core macroeconomic indicators—including gross domestic product, inflation, trade, and sectoral statistics—your field provides essential inputs to fiscal and monetary policy, federal transfers, and economic decision-making at all levels.
These outputs are not only foundational to Canada’s economic governance, but also to public confidence in the country’s economic performance and resilience.

Your work positions Statistics Canada as a trusted and responsive data partner across government, ensuring that decision-makers have access to timely, relevant, and high-quality data, while maintaining independence and confidentiality.

Delivering on these priorities will require explicit alignment of resources—including funding, workforce, and executive attention—with enterprise priorities, and disciplined trade-offs where activities do not support scaled implementation.
At the same time, the integrity, coherence, and credibility of Canada’s core economic statistics must be sustained.

In a context of fiscal constraint, evolving data sources, and increasing demand for timely insight, this means continuing to deliver mission-critical programs that directly inform monetary policy, fiscal transfers, and economic stability.
Strengthening how the value and impact of these statistics are communicated—linking outputs to real-world outcomes and public understanding—will be essential to reinforcing trust and relevance.
This includes advancing key initiatives such as the implementation of the System of National Accounts 2025 and the development of the TechStats program.
This also depends on sustaining a respectful, inclusive, and accountable workplace during a period of sustained change.
Workforce adjustment, skills transition, and modernization efforts require steady leadership grounded in fairness and clarity.

Advancing reconciliation in practical ways, strengthening inclusive practices, and reinforcing leadership accountability for supporting and developing people will be key to maintaining engagement and trust.
I encourage you to insist on clarity, maintain focus on outcomes, and model disciplined execution.
Where trade-offs are required, make them explicit.
Where timelines are set, manage actively to them.
Perfection is not the objective—timely, high-quality delivery is.

text: The Economic Statistics Field plays a central role in Canada’s economic governance.
Our programs produce the core macroeconomic statistics that underpin monetary and fiscal policy, federal transfers, legislative requirements, and public understanding of economic conditions.

In a context of fiscal restraint, heightened delivery expectations, shifting trade and geopolitical conditions, and accelerating technological change, our responsibility remains clear: to sustain trusted, high‑quality core outputs while continuing to modernize how we produce them.
This mandate sets out priorities that will guide our work over the coming year.
These priorities are intended to support focus and disciplined execution, with clear and transparent decision-making.
They require us to make explicit choices, so effort and resources are aligned to the highest value outcomes.
Integrating artificial intelligence and automation into statistical workflows

workforce_implications: reduce manual effort
work embedded directly into production workflows
clarify handoffs across programs

text: We will continue to integrate artificial intelligence and automation into statistical workflows and to streamline processes across the Generic Statistical Business Process Model. This work is intended to improve efficiency, reduce manual effort, and better support the ongoing production of core statistical programs. Emphasis will be placed on approaches that can be embedded directly into production workflows, reduce duplication, and clarify handoffs across programs. Automation and advanced methods, including artificial intelligence where it demonstrably adds value, will be applied to support reliable and repeatable production rather than experimentation alone. This work will continue to align with enterprise platforms and shared solutions and will be supported by appropriate governance, documentation, and monitoring. The objective is to strengthen the sustainability and consistency of production while maintaining quality, transparency, and public trust.

text: Our people are central to delivering on this mandate. We will continue to strengthen workforce sustainability by supporting employees and equipping managers to lead teams effectively through transitions while maintaining safe, respectful, and supportive work environments. In 2026/2027, this includes supporting employees and leaders through workforce adjustment pressures, skills transition in data, methods, and digital tools, and cultural change associated with modernization and evolving ways of working. The transition to new tools, methods, and data sources will require sustained attention to training, mentorship, and realistic sequencing of work alongside production demands. We will continue to strengthen leadership capacity among managers and supervisors, with emphasis on clarity of roles, responsibilities, and priorities in a constrained and changing environment. Clear communication, consistent performance management, and attention to employee well‑being will be essential to sustaining engagement, clarity, and trust. Managers are expected to work within prescribed timelines and to exercise disciplined decision‑making, fostering a culture of action over prolonged deliberation. Issues should be resolved at the appropriate level, with leaders taking ownership of decisions within their accountabilities.

text: The transition to open-source environments will continue as an important component of transformation across the field. In 2026/2027, this transition will focus on sustaining previous progress with greater emphasis on validation, upskilling and governance. Work will continue to prioritize reusable solutions and shared components, with development aligned to enterprise architecture to support interoperability, scalable solutions and long-term sustainability. Teams will be supported as they continue to adopt open‑source tools while meeting ongoing production responsibilities, including through training and collaborative development practices. This work will be guided by the need to maintain secure and stable production environments and the capacity required to support solutions over time. Decisions will reflect accountability for secure, stable, and reliable delivery.

Sustaining high-quality core economic statistics

text: At the centre of this mandate is our responsibility to deliver high‑quality, trusted core economic statistics in a timely manner. This responsibility is non‑negotiable and remains the primary consideration in setting priorities and allocating resources. This includes responsible data stewardship and ongoing efforts to improve how diverse forms of economic activity are reflected in official statistics. In 2026/2027, this includes the successful delivery of the 2026 Census of Agriculture. This major operation requires secure collection, processing, and dissemination; systems stability and operational resilience; and sustained public and stakeholder confidence. Its delivery will require careful management of fiscal, workforce and operational resources, as well as close coordination across the agency. We will continue to streamline operations and identify opportunities to strengthen quality, coherence, and consistency in cross-field collaboration. We will also advance implementation of the 2025 System of National Accounts to ensure comprehensive data and international relevance. The delivery of core outputs that support legislation, monetary policy, fiscal transfers, and economic decision‑making will remain the field’s foremost priority. Programs will continue to adapt to emerging analytical and policy needs. This includes strengthening measurement of artificial intelligence and emerging technologies through TechStat; providing timely and relevant insights on Canada–U.S. economic relations, including trade, tourism, investment, and ownership; and supporting key policy domains such as defense, energy, critical minerals, environmental and ecosystem accounting, and northern economic development. Increased use of administrative and alternative data sources will continue to support these efforts while managing respondent burden. Where capacity constraints require trade-offs, they will be made explicitly and transparently, with resources focused on protecting mission critical programs and maintaining public trust in Canada’s economic statistics.

text: Delivering on this mandate will require focus, discipline, and collective effort. It will also require strong critical thinking to ensure clarity about what we will not do, where simplification is necessary, and how resources are aligned in support of successful outcomes. Leaders at all levels are expected to manage actively to achieve timelines and delivery milestones, strengthen prioritization and accountability, and support timely decision‑making. This includes maintaining alignment with agreed priorities and ensuring decisions and actions support delivery. As we do so, we will maintain sound risk management and accountability for delivery while continuing to produce the high-quality statistics that Canadians rely on.

source_id: Social, Health and Labour Statistics Field_All staff_2
text:
Lead efforts to enhance housing statistics by producing high-quality information on housing supply, affordability, and outcomes. The field will improve the coverage, frequency, and timeliness of data on housing stock, residential construction and rental prices, and collaborate with Government of Canada partners to inform housing priorities.

The field will provide strategic leadership for the National Justice Statistics Initiative (NJSI), delivering authoritative information on crime, victimization and the administration of justice in Canada. In 2026/2027, you will advance the NJSI priority on Bail and Recontact Data Enhancement by standardizing definitions and data collection protocols and partnering with courts, corrections, law enforcement, and community organizations to improve data completeness and timeliness.

It will lead the delivery of the statistical indicators measuring progress under the Federal Provincial Territories Shared Health Priorities initiative, and oversee Statistics Canada’s contribution to the proposal for the new Health & Life Sciences Data, Research and Infrastructure Collaboratorium initiative. The field will also advance streamlining efforts within the Health Statistics Program to support the financial viability of the Canadian Health Measures Survey and continue implementing the Overdose Crisis Data Program to address critical data gaps.

The field will continue to deliver high-quality Quality-of-Life measures by addressing the remaining objectives identified in the 2024/2025 Biennial Review, launching the 2026/2027 Biennial Review and adopting recommendations from the program evaluation. As a field, we will also strengthen dissemination, analysis, and data discoverability through the Quality-of-Life Hub, including improvements to automation, data pipelines and interoperability. Across these areas, efforts will aim to improve timeliness, reduce production burden where possible, and enhance the accessibility and usefulness of outputs for decision-makers.

source_id: Social, Health and Labour Statistics Field_All staff_3
text: The field will advance transformation initiatives to modernize statistical production and support efficient, high-quality delivery in line with the December 2028 deadline. This will be achieved through your work in the transition to open-source environments by coordinating field activities, providing technical support, and managing milestones and risks in collaboration with enterprise partners. The field will transition programs to modern corporate platforms to enable integrated, metadata-driven pipelines that support automation and enterprise best practices, while maintaining the rigour and reliability of monthly production. As part of this work, Field 8 will deliver on the modernization of the Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours and the Labour Force Survey, simplifying and streamlining processing, improving data quality, reducing manual intervention, and strengthening program stewardship. Our field will advance the redesign of the General Social Statistics Program to meet the ever-increasing data needs. These efforts are expected to contribute to more efficient production processes, including reducing manual steps, supporting timelier outputs, and increasing opportunities for reuse through enterprise approaches.
